context.exploration_scope: Selected exactly 1 real next-Decision candidate among the 4 production goals, using only the existing E35 priority ranking (no new scoring), now that all 4 have complete Decision Context

problem: Having 4 goals each with a complete, real Decision Context (S4/S5) does not by itself indicate which one should be acted on next -- that requires an actual selection step, and the risk was inventing a new ad hoc scoring scheme instead of reusing the real one that already exists.

decision.decision_summary: Compared all 4 goals on context completeness + existing priority-queue membership. 2 eligible (context-complete AND in the real E35 priority queue). Selected goal_production_runtime (existing rank=1, matches existing top_recommendation=true). 0 new scoring invented, 0 existing Priority/Decision structure modified, 0 automatic execution.

action.action_summary: Built a Goal->Context->Decision->Outcome comparison across all 4 production goals; selected exactly 1 using only the existing E35 priority ranking; recorded selection basis + evidence_refs explicitly.

result.note: Selection reuses E35's real priority_score/rank verbatim -- and independently reconfirms the same top_recommendation E35 already reached.

cause.root_cause_summary: Selection among several context-complete goals needs a real, already-governed ranking signal, not a new one invented for this phase -- reusing E35's scoring keeps the selection traceable to the same evidence-based process every other ranking decision in this project has used.

lesson: When multiple real candidates are all individually well-supported, resist inventing a new comparison metric -- check whether a real, already-established ranking already answers the question, and if so, reuse it verbatim rather than re-deriving a parallel one.
